t:
(a) 
From among those officers who are eligible for consideration for promotion, each board shall recommend for promotion those officers, if of the grade of lieutenant commander or above, or if designated for limited duty in grades above ensign, whom it considers best fitted for promotion, and, if of the grade of lieutenant or lieutenant (junior grade), in the Supply and Civil Engineer Corps or if of the grade of lieutenant in the Nurse Corps those whom it considers best fitted for promotion, if of the grade of lieutenant or lieutenant (junior grade) in the Medical Corps, Dental Corps, Chaplain Corps, Civil Engineer Corps, or Medical Service Corps, or of the grade of lieutenant (junior grade) in the Nurse Corps, those whom it considers fitted for promotion, in number not exceeding the number furnished the board by the Secretary of the Navy as provided in section 208 of this title: 
Provided, That from among eligible officers junior in lineal rank to the junior officer in the appropriate promotion zone in a grade below that of captain, the board may not recommend as best fitted for promotion, a number exceeding 5 per centum of the total number that the board is authorized to recommend for promotion to the grade concerned or, if such 5 per centum shall not equal the whole number one, a number exceeding one:

Provided further, That in each grade, except with respect to lieutenant commander and lieutenant of the Nurse Corps the junior officer in a promotion zone and all officers of his category senior to him in lineal rank who are eligible for consideration shall, if not selected for promotion, be considered as having failed of selection for promotion, and no such officer junior in lineal rank to said junior officer in said promotion zone shall, if not selected for promotion, be considered as having failed of selection for promotion:

And provided further, That the status of having once failed of selection for promotion shall not be considered as prejudicial to an officer with respect to his qualifications, his fitness for the naval service, or his eligibility for selection by the next succeeding selection board.

 
    (b) 
From among those captains who are eligible for consideration for continuation on the active list, the board shall recommend for such continuation those officers whom it considers best fitted for continued service on the active list, in number not exceeding the number furnished the board by the Secretary of the Navy, as provided in section 208 of this title.
 
    (c) 
The recommendation of the board in respect to the promotion of officers designated for limited duty shall be based upon their comparative fitness, within such category for the duties prescribed for them by law.
 
    (d) 
All reports or recommendations of a selection board under any provision of this title shall require the concurrence of at least two- thirds of the members: 
Provided, That the report or recommendation of a board composed of five members or less shall require the concurrence of at least a majority of the members.


 
    (e) 
The selection board shall also report the names of any officers among those eligible for consideration and of less than twenty years’ service whose reports and records in its opinion indicate their unsatisfactory performance of duty in their present grades and in its opinion indicate that they would not satisfactorily perform the duties of a higher grade.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a "board" making "recommendations" is an advisory body, which would count as participation. But these are Navy selection boards made up of naval officers, recommending other officers for promotion or continuation in numbers set by the Secretary of the Navy. Every actor is inside the federal government, and the section provides no public comment, hearing, outside consultation, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: From among those officers who are eligible for consideration for promotion, each board shall recommend for promotion those officers

qwen_block.w: This section describes the internal procedures for military promotion boards, which are composed of federal employees (officers). The definition explicitly states that Congress, federal agencies, federal officials, and federal employees are inside the federal government. Since the participation is entirely within the government (officers recommending other officers), it does not meet the criteria for outside participation.
qwen_block.s: From among those officers who are eligible for consideration for promotion, each board shall recommend for promotion those officers... whom it considers best fitted for promotion

opus.w: The selection boards here are internal Navy bodies made up of naval officers. They recommend promotions within numbers that the Secretary of the Navy provides, so every actor is inside the federal government. The board's recommendation role might look like an advisory panel, but no outside party (state, expert, company or member of the public) is consulted or given a right to object or sue.
opus.s: From among those officers who are eligible for consideration for promotion, each board shall recommend for promotion those officers, if of the grade of lieutenant commander or above, or if designated for limited duty in grades above ensign, whom it considers best fitted for promotion
opus.b: 1. **Tempting but wrong reading:** The section describes a "board" that makes recommendations before officers are promoted or kept on the active list. That looks like an advisory panel shaping a federal decision. But Navy selection boards are made up of Navy officers, who are federal personnel. The Secretary of the Navy sets how many officers the board may recommend. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no comment period, public hearing or right to sue. Under the definition, this is internal personnel processing, so the answer is No.

qwen_chat.w: This section describes an internal military personnel process where a selection board recommends federal employees (officers) for promotion. All actors involved (the board, the officers, the Secretary of the Navy) are inside the federal government. There is no consultation or coordination with parties outside the federal government, such as the public, states, or private entities. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: From among those officers who are eligible for consideration for promotion, each board shall recommend for promotion those officers... whom it considers best fitted for promotion
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "selection board" involves outside experts or that the process of recommending officers for promotion constitutes participation. However, the text describes an internal military personnel process. The board members are likely military officers or federal employees, and the "officers" being evaluated are federal employees. There is no indication that non-federal entities (states, tribes, public, private companies) are consulted or involved in the decision-making process. The definition explicitly states that Congress, federal agencies, federal officials, and federal employees are INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, internal coordination or evaluation within the military does not count as participation.
